Are these the same certificate number? The register form "R060/2000-NL1-2012.40" vs document "R60/2000-NL1-12-40". The "R060" vs "R60" — OIML R60 is the recommendation; sometimes written R060 with leading zero padding. "NL1" is the issuer. "2012.40" vs "12-40" — the year 2012 abbreviated to 12, and separator differences (.40 vs -40). Also the register id comment says cert_id: 3026 and num: R060/2000-NL1-2012.40, and source_pdf is "r060-2000-nl1-2012-40.pdf" — the filename uses hyphens consistently.

So this is clearly the same certificate with format differences: R60 vs R060 (leading zero), 2012 vs 12 (year abbreviation), .40 vs -40 (separator). Per the rules: "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form."

Verdict: same-entity, best_value: "R060/2000-NL1-2012.40" (register's canonical form).

One short sentence for why: The two strings denote the same OIML R60 certificate (leading-zero padding, 2-digit vs 4-digit year, and separator drift), so use the register's canonical form.
